agentContributions.notes: Novel story — Live Preview is a new capability. The codegraph confirms useContent (236 callers) is the single attachment point: ContentstackLink, ContentstackImage, ContentstackTable, and ContentstackContentCards all call useContent().getContentByKey(). Plugging live-preview reactivity into useContent propagates updates to all consumers with zero per-component changes. ContentstackContext.tsx is the second attachment point for SDK initialization. Contentstack APIs are unreachable at test time; all VCs stop at our boundary with explicit mock assumptions. Prior flags addressed: (1) codebase access used to locate attachment points, (2) VCs elaborated from description since ACs are empty, (3) real-time complexity bounded by stating assumptions about mocked Contentstack client behavior.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Pipeline data inconsistency: coordinatorReview references speckit authoring 15 acceptance criteria, but speckit is absent from both appliedAgents and agentContributions — only openspec was recorded. Either speckit's output was never persisted or the coordinator review was written against phantom data. openspec provided valuable architectural insight (useContent as single attachment point with 236 callers, downstream propagation strategy) but failed its core AC-elaboration mandate: acceptanceChanged=false, splitCount=0, for a novel story that started with empty ACs. The architectural notes are useful but do not substitute for acceptance criteria. Even if speckit's 15 ACs exist somewhere, they were authored without codebase access (explicitly stated), inferring structure from naming conventions for a complex real-time, multi-locale (GO/UP/MX) live-preview feature involving WebSocket/polling, token schemes, and preview-vs-published state synchronization. This is high-risk unvalidated inference. The collaborative pipeline structure was correct in intent but incomplete in execution, and the output needs human validation against the actual codebase before implementation.
